content_snapshot: Complete familiarization/practice sessions before testing
Warm up with submaximal repetitions of the exercise
Select initial weight at ~50-70% of perceived capacity
Attempt the lift with proper form
If successful, rest 3-5 minutes and increase weight
Repeat until failure occurs (unable to complete lift with proper form)
Record the last successfully completed weight as the 1-RM
Complete within 4 trials to avoid fatigue

content_snapshot: Get into a position that facilitates relaxation. Move to the point in the ROM where you experience a sensation of mild discomfort. If performing partner-assisted PNF stretching, communicate clearly with your partner. Hold stretches for 15 to 30 seconds. Repeat unilateral stretches on both sides. Decrease stretch intensity if you experience pain, radiating symptoms, or loss of sensation. Use caution when stretching a hypermobile joint. Avoid combination movements that involve the spine (e.g., extension and lateral flexion). Stabilizing muscles should be active to protect other joints and prevent unwanted movements.

content_snapshot: A logical sequence, although there are some variations, is to administer tests in this order: 1. Nonfatiguing tests (e.g., height, weight, flexibility, skinfolds and girth measurements, vertical jump) 2. Agility tests (e.g., T-test, 5-10-5 test, 5-0-5 test, Illinois test) 3. Maximum power and strength tests (e.g., 1RM power clean, 1RM squat, 1RM bench press) 4. Sprint tests (e.g., 40 m sprint with split times at 10 m and 20 m) 5. Local muscular endurance tests (e.g., push-up test, partial curl-up, YMCA bench press test)
